operation_details.summary: To approve within Slack, you need:

parameters.name: Response Type
parameters.description: set to Approval

options.name: Capture Who Responded
options.description: turn this on to switch the approval buttons to Slack interactive buttons and record who responded. The remaining settings appear once it's on

options.name: Restrict Who Can Approve
options.description: select the users allowed to act. You can also specify user IDs with an expression. Anyone not on the list who clicks gets a private notice, and the workflow keeps waiting

options.name: Unauthorized Reply
options.description: the private (ephemeral) message shown to someone who clicks but isn't on the approver list. Defaults to You are not authorized to respond to this request

options.name: After Decision
options.description: what happens to the original Slack message once someone approves or declines

operation_details.operation: When you get link buttons instead
operation_details.summary: The node behaves as before, sending buttons that open an n8n confirmation page, when any of these apply:

parameters.name: Response Type
parameters.description: is Free Text or Custom Form

parameters.name: Capture Who Responded
parameters.description: is off

parameters.name: The buttons don't do anything, or Slack shows a warning
parameters.description: the Request URL is wrong, your instance isn't publicly reachable over HTTPS, or the Signature Secret is missing or wrong. Slack shows the same warning for a rejected callback as for an unreachable URL

parameters.name: Someone gets a "not authorized" reply
parameters.description: that user isn't listed in Restrict Who Can Approve. The wording comes from Unauthorized Reply

parameters.name: The workflow never resumes although someone responded
parameters.description: the Signature Secret is missing or doesn't match your app's Signing Secret. n8n rejects callbacks it can't verify, and the workflow keeps waiting
